capabilities: Sync notes, attachments and .obsidian configuration across devices
Resolve conflicts with keep local, keep remote, keep both or three-way Markdown merge
Share notes and folders by link and publish public blogs
Collaborate on Markdown notes through invitations and live updates
Manage files in a web console with history, diffs, restore and recycle bin
disambiguation: Not an object-storage (S3/OSS) client; it syncs to its own self-hosted Go server.
extras: Requires deploying and running a separate Go server (Linux binary/systemd, Docker, or runtime package); community plugin settings sync uploads full data.json files that may contain credentials; WASM and executable server extensions run with host or server-account access and should only be installed after review.
problem: Users who want their vault synced through a server they run themselves, with note sharing and a public blog from the same place, have no self-hosted option.
summary: Self-hosted sync server and Obsidian client that keeps notes, attachments and config in sync across devices, with sharing, blog publishing and collaboration.
